info.description: This is the API documentation for the backend service
info.title: Backend API

get.description: Returns one page of the caller's keys, newest first. The key itself is never returned, only its prefix. An admin can pass all=true for the keys of every user, or user_id for one user; for any other role both are 403 (except the caller's own user_id). A request authenticated with an API key is refused (403).

parameters.description: Admin only: the keys of all users
parameters.name: all

parameters.description: Admin only: the keys of one user
parameters.name: user_id

post.description: Creates a key for the caller. The key has the role of its owner at the time of each request (a demoted owner's keys are demoted). An expiry is required: set expires_at (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC3339) or expires_in_days, not both, at most 365 days ahead by default. The caller can have 25 active keys by default (409 above that). The raw key (sk_ and 64 hex characters) is returned once in raw_key, with Cache-Control no-store, and cannot be retrieved again; only its SHA-256 is stored. A request authenticated with an API key is refused (403): manage keys with a login session. Unknown request fields are refused. An Idempotency-Key header is ignored on this route (also with IDEMPOTENCY_ENABLED=true): the response holds the raw key, which the idempotency module must never store.

delete.description: Deletes (revokes) a key at once: it stops authenticating with the next request and the WebSocket connections opened with it close with code 1008. A user can delete their own keys; an admin can delete any key. A key of another user, for a caller who is not an admin, is 404 like a key that does not exist. A request authenticated with an API key is refused (403).

get.description: Returns one page of audit entries, newest first. Admin only, with a login session (an API key is refused with 403); the caller must still be an enabled admin in the database. Filters: user_id, action, entity_type, entity_id and a time range (start_date, end_date: RFC3339 with a zone, inclusive); an invalid value is 400. Paging: limit (default 25, at most 100) and offset (at most 100000), or the next_cursor of the previous page (keyset paging for deep pages; the cursor ignores offset and the answer has no exact total). An entry holds the action, the entity, the user and details (method, route, status, client IP, request ID and small values such as the old and new role); never a request or response body, header, password or key.

parameters.description: Filter by entity type (lower case words with underscores)
parameters.name: entity_type

parameters.description: Filter by action (lower case words with underscores)
parameters.name: action

parameters.description: next_cursor of the previous page (overrides offset)
parameters.name: cursor

post.description: Authenticate with username and password; returns a JWT access token and the user. With refresh sessions on, the login starts a session: the access token lives ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRATION and carries the session ID (sid), and the response sets the httpOnly refresh_token cookie (named __Host-refresh_token unless SECURE_COOKIES=false; Path /, SameSite=Strict, Secure unless SECURE_COOKIES=false) for POST /api/v1/auth/refresh; without them the token lives JWT_EXPIRATION. With refresh sessions on, the request needs the X-Requested-With header (any value) and must not be cross-site (403), and its Content-Type must be application/json (415); both are checked first (login CSRF protection). Every credential failure (unknown user, wrong password, disabled account, SSO-only account) answers the same 401 "Invalid username or password". After 5 failed attempts for one username within 15 minutes, every login for that username answers 429 with Retry-After for 15 minutes. While attempts for the same username are in flight and use up its slots, a further attempt answers 429 with Retry-After 1. Only the submitted username answers 429: when the found account itself is locked or busy (the same account under another spelling of the name), the answer is the generic 401, so no answer shows whether a name is an account.

parameters.description: Required with refresh sessions on (any value, for example XMLHttpRequest)
parameters.name: X-Requested-With

post.description: Ends the sessions that the request proves: the session of the refresh token cookie and the session (sid) of a valid bearer token. It revokes their refresh tokens, blocks the sessions so that all their access tokens get 401, blocks the presented access token until its expiry, closes the WebSockets opened with it and deletes the cookie. Other sessions of the user keep working. An expired or invalid bearer token is ignored. A request without a cookie and without a valid bearer token ends nothing and answers 200; a repeated logout answers 200. The request needs the X-Requested-With header (any value) and must not be cross-site; otherwise 403. When a lookup, revoke or block fails, the other steps still run and the cookie is deleted, but the answer is 500.

parameters.description: Any value (CSRF protection), for example XMLHttpRequest
parameters.name: X-Requested-With

post.description: Ends every session of the current user: revokes all their refresh tokens, blocks every session that can still hold a live access token, writes a user block that rejects every access token issued up to now, blocks the presented access token, closes all WebSockets of the user and deletes the cookie. A login after the answer works. It is idempotent. When a step fails, the other steps still run and the answer is 500.

403.description: An API key cannot end the sessions

get.description: Returns the authenticated user. A disabled account answers 401, a deleted one 404.

put.description: Changes the password of the signed-in local user. Login session only (an API key is refused with 403). The body needs the current password and the new one (at least 8 characters, at most 72 bytes, not equal to the current one); unknown fields are refused. A wrong current password answers 401 "Current password is incorrect" and counts toward the same per-account failure lock as the password login (5 failures within 15 minutes lock the account for 15 minutes; the locked account answers 429 with Retry-After, also for the right password). A user with no local password (an SSO account) gets 400; with OIDC as the only interactive login (OIDC_LOCAL_AUTH=false) only the service account may change a password (403 otherwise); a disabled user gets 401. On success only the password hash is written and every other session of the user ends: their refresh tokens are revoked and their sessions are blocked, so their access tokens get 401; the open WebSockets of those sessions are closed by the next revalidation (within about a minute). The current session keeps working: its cookie, its access token and its socket are not touched. API keys are kept: delete them separately when the old password may have been exposed. The entry of the audit log has the action change_password and never holds a password. When the password was stored but a revocation step failed, the answer is 500, the new password stands and the entry has revocation_failed; end the remaining sessions with logout-all or change the password again. The login rate limit (LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT per client IP) applies.

403.description: An API key cannot change a password, or password sign-in is disabled for the account

get.description: The identity provider sends the browser here with a code and the state. The state works once and only from the browser that started the login (the oidc_binding cookie); the code is exchanged with the PKCE verifier; the ID token is validated (signature, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce). The account is found by issuer and sub, or created with auth_provider oidc and the role user (admin when a role of the OIDC_ADMIN_ROLES claim matches exactly); an existing OIDC account gets its role from the claim at every login. An existing local account is never linked or taken over. On success the answer sets the httpOnly refresh_token cookie (named __Host-refresh_token unless SECURE_COOKIES=false) and redirects (302) to the fixed web UI path OIDC_FRONTEND_PATH, without any token in the URL; the web UI then calls POST /api/v1/auth/refresh for its access token. Every refusal caused by the request or the provider answers 400 {"error":"Login failed"}. A provider that does not answer, answers with a server error, or refuses this server's client credentials (a configuration problem, logged at Error level) answers 502.

parameters.description: Authorization code from the identity provider
parameters.name: code

parameters.description: Error code from the identity provider (the login is refused)
parameters.name: error

get.description: Redirects the browser to the identity provider (authorization code flow with PKCE S256, a random state and a nonce). The state, the PKCE verifier and the nonce are kept on the server for OIDC_STATE_TTL and work once; a short-lived httpOnly cookie (oidc_binding, with the __Host- prefix unless SECURE_COOKIES=false; SameSite=Lax, Path /) ties the login to this browser. Answers 404 unless AUTH_ENABLED and OIDC_ENABLED are true. No parameter of the request is used.

post.description: Sends a mail with a single-use reset link to the local account with this username, when the account exists, is enabled, has an email address, is not a service account (the bootstrap admin) and is not an SSO account. Public. Only available when PASSWORD_RESET_ENABLED=true (otherwise 404). The answer is always 202 with the same body, whether or not the account exists or got a mail (an unknown, ineligible, throttled or mailed account, and a mail failure, cannot be told apart by the status, the body, the headers or the time): the lookup and the send run after the answer. At most one mail per account in PASSWORD_RESET_MIN_INTERVAL; a request in that time sends nothing. The link is PASSWORD_RESET_URL + /reset-password#token=... and the token is valid for PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_TTL. A request that asks again replaces the unused earlier token. Unknown fields are refused. It has its own LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT budget per client IP. No cookie is set or read.

400.description: No username, a username that cannot exist, or an invalid body

404.description: The password reset is not enabled

post.description: Sets a new password with the token from the mail. Public. Only available when PASSWORD_RESET_ENABLED=true (otherwise 404). The password follows the password rules (at least 8 characters, at most 72 bytes) and is checked first: a bad password answers 400 and does not use up the token. Then the token is consumed atomically (single use: of two requests with the same token exactly one succeeds) and the new password is stored. A token that is malformed, unknown, used or expired, or of an account that was disabled, deleted, turned into a service account or lost its email address, answers one generic 400 "Invalid or expired token". On success (204, no body) every session of the user ends the way an admin password reset ends it: the refresh tokens are revoked, every access token issued before is rejected (user block), the open WebSockets are closed and the failed-login lock of the account is cleared; the account can sign in with the new password at once, also when it was locked. API keys are kept: delete them separately when the account may have been exposed. The audit log gets an entry with the action password_reset (actor and entity: the account). When the password was stored but a revocation step failed, the answer is 500, the new password stands and the entry has revocation_failed. Unknown fields are refused. It has its own LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT budget per client IP. No cookie is set or read.
post.summary: Set a new password with a reset token

parameters.description: The token and the new password
parameters.name: request

400.description: Invalid or expired token, or a password that breaks the rules (the token is not used up)

404.description: The password reset is not enabled

post.description: Issues a new access token for the session of the refresh token cookie and rotates the refresh token (the old one is consumed, a new cookie is set). The request needs the X-Requested-With header (any value) and must not be cross-site; otherwise 403. A session ends SESSION_MAX_LIFETIME after login and SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT after its last login or refresh; rotation never extends it, and the access token never outlives it. A token rotated less than REFRESH_REUSE_GRACE ago (two tabs refreshing at once) gets one more access token, once, without a new cookie. Any other reuse of a consumed token revokes the session and blocks its access tokens. A session that started before a user block (logout-all, a role change, disabling or deleting the user) is refused and revoked even when its refresh token was still active. The refresh cookie is named __Host-refresh_token unless SECURE_COOKIES=false (then refresh_token) and has Path /. Every refusal answers the same 401 and deletes the cookie.

parameters.description: Any value (CSRF protection), for example XMLHttpRequest
parameters.name: X-Requested-With

post.description: Self-registration of a local account with the role user. Only available when SELF_REGISTRATION is true; otherwise 404. Role, disabled, provider and service account fields in the body are ignored. The username is 3 to 100 characters (letters, digits and . _ - @, starting with a letter or digit); the password is at least 8 characters and at most 72 bytes.

get.description: Get a list of all items. Sort with sort and order; without them the order is id ascending. Rows with an equal sort value are ordered by id in the same direction, so pages never repeat or skip a row. The X-Total-Count header holds the number of items that match the filter, ignoring limit and offset; the body is a plain array.

X-Total-Count.description: Number of items that match the filter, ignoring limit and offset

post.description: Create a new item with the provided information. With IDEMPOTENCY_ENABLED=true the request may carry an Idempotency-Key header: the same key with the same request replays the stored response (header Idempotency-Replayed: true) and creates no second item, the same key with another request is 422 and while the first request still runs it is 409 with Retry-After. A response that is a 5xx or 499 is not stored, so the client can retry.

parameters.description: Optional key (1 to 255 printable ASCII characters) that makes the request safe to retry; used only with IDEMPOTENCY_ENABLED=true
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

409.description: Duplicate, or a request with the same Idempotency-Key is still in progress (Retry-After)

422.description: The Idempotency-Key was used with a different request

get.description: Get an item by its ID

delete.description: Delete an item by its ID

get.description: Returns one page of jobs of the queue (optional module, JOBS_ENABLED=true; the route does not exist otherwise), newest first unless sort and order say otherwise. Rows with an equal sort value are ordered by id in the same direction, so pages never repeat or skip a row. Never the payload: a job shows its type, status, attempts, schedule, the worker that holds it and the text of the last error. Admin only with AUTH_ENABLED=true. A read: no audit entry.

Returns the display values of the web UI: the product title (APP_TITLE), whether authentication is enabled (AUTH_ENABLED), whether the single sign-on login is offered (oidc_enabled: AUTH_ENABLED and OIDC_ENABLED) and whether the password form is shown (local_auth_enabled: AUTH_ENABLED, and OIDC off or OIDC_LOCAL_AUTH) and whether the web UI offers the password reset by mail (password_reset_enabled: PASSWORD_RESET_ENABLED with the password form shown; false while the two routes do not exist). Public in both auth modes: no authentication, so the login page can use it. Cached for 5 minutes.

Returns one page of users, ordered by username unless sort says otherwise, never with a password hash. Rows with an equal sort value are ordered by id in the same direction, so pages never repeat or skip a row. Admin only, with a login session (an API key is refused with 403); the caller must still be an enabled admin in the database. Filter by role (exact) or search (username, display name or email contains the text).

parameters.description: Text in the username, display name or email (at most 100 characters)
parameters.name: search

post.description: Creates a local user with the given role. Admin only, with a login session. The username is 3 to 100 characters (ASCII letters, digits and . _ - @, starting with a letter or digit), the password at least 8 characters and at most 72 bytes; the role is required. A display name that is empty defaults to the username. Unknown request fields are refused. A username that exists is 409. The response never holds the password or its hash. With IDEMPOTENCY_ENABLED=true the request may carry an Idempotency-Key header: the same key with the same request replays the stored response (header Idempotency-Replayed: true) and creates no second user.

parameters.description: Optional key (1 to 255 printable ASCII characters) that makes the request safe to retry; used only with IDEMPOTENCY_ENABLED=true
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

409.description: A username that exists, or a request with the same Idempotency-Key is still in progress (Retry-After)

422.description: The Idempotency-Key was used with a different request

get.description: Returns one user, never with a password hash. Admin only, with a login session. A malformed ID is 400, an unknown one 404.

put.description: Changes the display name, the email and/or the password of a user. Admin only, with a login session. Only these fields are accepted; any other field (role, disabled, username, ...) is refused with 400, because role and disabled have endpoints of their own that enforce the last-admin rule and end the user's sessions. A password can be set only for a local user (400 otherwise); setting it ends every session of the user (access tokens issued before are rejected, refresh tokens are revoked, WebSockets are closed) and keeps the API keys. The display name and email of an SSO user are overwritten by the identity provider at the next login. The response never holds a password or hash. With the password reset module on, a changed email address (or a new password) also deletes the user's unused reset tokens.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a user. Admin only, with a login session; the caller must still be an enabled admin in the database (403). The last enabled admin cannot be deleted (409, answered before anything is blocked when the admin deletes themselves); an admin may delete themselves when another enabled admin exists. The user's access ends: access tokens issued before are rejected (user block), refresh tokens are revoked, all their API keys are deleted and the WebSockets are closed. The user block is written before the delete (a failure answers 500 and deletes nothing, so the request can be repeated; a delete that the transaction guard refuses after a race, 403 or 409, has still blocked the user's tokens issued so far) and again after it (best effort); when a later step fails the answer is 500 and the user is gone.

put.description: Disables (disabled=true) or enables (disabled=false) a user. Admin only, with a login session; the caller must still be an enabled admin in the database (403). The last enabled admin cannot be disabled (409); an admin may disable themselves when another enabled admin exists. Disabling ends every session of the user: access tokens issued before it are rejected (user block), refresh tokens are revoked and the WebSockets are closed. The user's API keys are kept but stop authenticating while the owner is disabled. Enabling writes no new block: tokens issued before the disable stay rejected, and a login after the enable works. A request that does not change the state is a no-op (changed=false, no audit entry; a repeated disable still ends the sessions). Unknown request fields are refused. With the password reset module on, disabling also deletes the user's unused reset tokens.

Sets the role of a user. Admin only, with a login session; the caller must still be an enabled admin in the database (403). The last enabled admin cannot be demoted (409); an admin may demote themselves when another enabled admin exists. An unchanged role changes nothing (changed=false, no audit entry) but ends the sessions of the user again, so repeating a request whose answer was 500 finishes the revocation. A change ends every session of the user: access tokens issued before it are rejected (user block), refresh tokens are revoked and the WebSockets are closed, so the next request needs a new login that carries the new role; the user's API keys stay and use the new role at once. The role of an SSO user is set by the identity provider at each login (OIDC_ADMIN_ROLES, OIDC_DEVOPS_ROLES) and can override this change: the response has idp_managed=true. The user block is retried a few times; when the change committed but a revocation step still failed, the answer is 500 and the change stands: repeat the same request to finish the revocation. Unknown request fields are refused.
put.summary: Change the role of a user

get.description: Upgrades the HTTP connection to a WebSocket for real-time events. With AUTH_ENABLED=false no credential is needed and any topic can be subscribed. With AUTH_ENABLED=true the upgrade needs one credential: `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, `X-API-Key: sk_<key>` (header only), or `?token=<jwt>` for browsers (removed from the URL before any logging). The upgrade runs the checks of the HTTP auth (token, session and user blocklists, a deleted or disabled user, an unknown, deleted or expired key) and counts against the per-IP RATE_LIMIT. A failed blocklist or user lookup refuses the upgrade (500). A socket over the per-user and per-key limit (WS_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_USER, default 16) is closed with code 1008 right after the upgrade. An open socket is closed with code 1008 on logout, logout-all, a disable, delete, role change or password reset of the user, a deleted key, and when the token or key expires; a periodic re-check closes the sockets that another replica revoked. Subscriptions are authorised: items and item:<id> for every user, user:<id> for that user (and admins), admin:<name> for admins; any other topic is ignored.

current_password.description: CurrentPassword is the password that the account has now.

new_password.description:
NewPassword is the new password: at least 8 characters, at most 72 bytes,
and not the current one.

role.description: Role is the new role: "user", "devops" or "admin".

changed.description:
Changed is false when the user already had the role (a no-op: nothing
is revoked and no audit entry is written).

idp_managed.description:
IDPManaged is true for an SSO user: the identity provider sets the role
at each login (OIDC_ADMIN_ROLES and OIDC_DEVOPS_ROLES), so this change
can be overridden at the next login.

prefix.description:
Prefix is the first 16 hex characters of the key (not secret enough to
use alone): it identifies the key in the list.

raw_key.description: RawKey is "sk_" and 64 hex characters, shown once.

message.example: If the account exists and can receive mail, a reset link has been sent.

new_password.description: NewPassword is the new password: at least 8 characters, at most 72 bytes.

token.description: Token is the token from the link of the mail (the fragment of the URL).

username.description: Username is the name of the local account that forgot its password.

disabled.description: Disabled is required: true disables the user, false enables them.

changed.description: Changed is false when the user already had that state.

auth_enabled.description: AuthEnabled tells the UI whether to show the login flow (AUTH_ENABLED).

local_auth_enabled.description:
LocalAuthEnabled tells the UI to show the username and password form:
AUTH_ENABLED, and OIDC off or OIDC_LOCAL_AUTH=true. With OIDC on and
OIDC_LOCAL_AUTH=false only a service account (the bootstrap admin) can
still log in with a password, through the API.

oidc_enabled.description:
OIDCEnabled tells the UI to offer the single sign-on button
(AUTH_ENABLED and OIDC_ENABLED).

password_reset_enabled.description:
PasswordResetEnabled tells the UI to offer "Forgot password?" and the
pages behind it: PASSWORD_RESET_ENABLED, with auth on and the password
form shown (local_auth_enabled). It is false whenever the two routes do
not exist (404).

password.description: Password is only for a local user (400 for an SSO user).

prefix.description: Prefix is the first APIKeyPrefixLen characters of the raw key.

version.description: For optimistic locking (1 = initial; 0 = not provided)

attempts.description: Attempts is the number of claims: a crash of a worker counts.

finished_at.description: FinishedAt is set when the job became succeeded or dead.

id.description: ID is the auto increment key.

last_error.description:
LastError is the error text of the last failed attempt, cut to
JobLastErrorMaxChars characters.

locked_by.description:
LockedBy is the worker (replica ID and worker number) that holds the
lease. Empty when the job is not running.

locked_until.description: LockedUntil is the end of the lease of a running job.

max_attempts.description: MaxAttempts is the number of claims after which a failing job is dead.

run_at.description: RunAt is when the job is due.

type.description: Type is the registered handler name.

external_id.description:
ExternalID is the subject at the identity provider; nil for a local
user. (auth_provider, external_id) is unique; MySQL allows many NULLs.

service_account.description:
ServiceAccount marks a local account that may still sign in with a
password when OIDC is the only interactive login (break-glass).

ApiKeyAuth.description: With AUTH_ENABLED=true: an API key (sk_ and 64 hex characters) from POST /api/v1/api-keys. Not accepted on the key, user and audit log management routes, on logout-all or on the password change.
ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key

BearerAuth.description: With AUTH_ENABLED=true: "Bearer <access token>" from POST /api/v1/auth/login or /api/v1/auth/refresh. Not used with AUTH_ENABLED=false.
BearerAuth.name: Authorization
